correctness.rationale: Uniform start makes a contribution to the zero Fourier mode pass from zero back to zero, so excursions past mode three require at least eight propulsion multipliers; the degree-six moment and log-moment jets are exactly those of the seven-mode truncation, for every time. Its positive a,b,c ensure an isolated eigenvalue at zero. On a sufficiently small complex k disk the analytic projection has nonzero initial/terminal overlap, and the other spectral part decays relative to it uniformly. Taking the local logarithm and differentiating gives t times the eigenvalue derivatives plus O(1), without assuming a gap for high modes. An independently expanded Schur complement gives λ=p/[2(a+λ−p/(4(b+λ−p/(4(c+λ)))))] with p=v²k² and D=0, reproducing all three rates. The independent Brownian term is exactly Dk². For b=a/2 the first two raw moments of Y=cos Δ are m and q=(3+m)/4. Nonnegative (1±Y)(Y−z)² give the sharp third-moment bounds by completing the square; their two-point equality laws have the same m,q, so mixing fills the interval. At m=−3/4 these reduce to the point mass at Y=−3/4 (zero weights are allowed). The upper bound for w=m₃ is strictly below 1 for m<1, so c>0 throughout. The lower endpoint minus the target is (m−1)(7m+5)/[4(1+m)] and the upper endpoint is strictly above the target. At m=−5/7 equality forces support {−1,−1/2} with masses 3/7 and 4/7, whose symmetric angular lift is unique.
residual_risks: The result is for stationary uniform initial angle and positive first-three harmonic relaxation rates; vanishing angular gaps outside those modes need not imply usual mixing properties.
Cancellation means vanishing linear cumulant rates, not finite-time Gaussianity or higher-order cancellation.

value.rationale: Matching the diffusion rate or cancelling long-time kurtosis leaves genuine higher-order differences. The theorem says exactly when a physically realizable angle law can remove the next even cumulant growth, gives both feasible signs away from the obstruction, and identifies the unique extremal design. The sharp bound over all turning probability laws is the distinctive value beyond expanding a Fourier hierarchy.
residual_risks: The finding does not identify all higher-order or finite-time departures from normality.
